correctness.rationale: For arbitrary finite nonempty P, negation is absence of an upward U-point in each principal upset; double negation requires all maxima above p in U. This gives exactly \(2^m\) fixed points. A WEM assignment colors the maximal points monochromatically within each comparability component; choosing empty or an upset containing all maxima counts \(W=\prod_i(1+u(P_i\setminus M_i))\). Their intersection has size \(2^c\). The remaining two-by-two cells follow by inclusion-exclusion. The proof constructs explicit neither-case witnesses from a bad maximal cone or two interacting nontrivial components; the converse follows because a proper nonempty maximal subset forces absence of every nonmaximal point in the uniquely allowed mixed component. Exhaustive independent pseudocomplement enumeration checked all 4473 labelled posets of orders 1..5.

value.rationale: The relative behavior of WEM and double-negation elimination is explicitly singled out as an example in arXiv:2110.11515 §6.6. The new theorem supplies an all-finite-Heyting-algebra joint distribution and classifies exactly those dual frames on which the two individual laws exhaust every valuation. These are natural relative semantic invariants that neither a separate gap theorem nor a Boolean-center census supplies, and the result gives an exact finite-poset computation without limiting the scope to a manufactured subfamily.
